Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Written August 27, 2026, following up the August 23 Sunday piece and covering material through August 25 and market prices through August 27. Host only. No new claims.

  • Sunday said: the crowd had flipped to Jordi on Bitcoin, hits 80,000 closed at 87.0%, and red August was already stressed, with five days still to go after this recap.
  • Since then: the 80,000 up-strike printed 0.9995 on Monday and left the feed. That is a Polymarket resolution, not a spot print. Gets down to 60,000 went from 34.5% to 28.5%.
  • The 10-year 5% line faded again. Sunday close 23.5% to 16.5%. Last midweek's archive high is gone.
  • Gold took more of the 2026 race. Gold wins 2026 25.0% to 31.5%. S&P wins 2026 57.5% to 53.5%.

What Sunday said to watch, and what happened

Sunday's week-ahead list was September 1 for red August, September 16 for hike versus hold, Jackson Hole on August 28, a couple more weeks above the 200-day, the year-end time-stop, and two pending prints (a vol series and a mid-70s confirm). Nothing on that list has resolved. Jackson Hole is still Friday. Red August still needs a monthly close.

The Bitcoin read is the one that moved. Sunday already had the 80,000 line at 87.0% and said not to invent a spot high from that jump. This window the up-strike went to 0.9995 at 2026-08-24 1:11 p.m. ET and then disappeared from the snapshot feed. The 75,000 up-strike had already done the same. That is stronger than Sunday's "pending a mid-70s tape confirm." It is still not a print of 80,000 or 81,000 dollars. Do not treat it as one.

Ben dated the follow-through himself, after Sunday, in Ethereum: Dubious Speculation:

"If we follow through this week, that would make the case for the low being in far stronger"

— Ben, August 23, 23:15

"This two-week candle for Bitcoin isn't going to close for another seven days."

— Ben, August 23, 24:02

That candle still has not closed. About August 30. He also said Bitcoin is up about 23%, above the bull-market support band, and that it was also above it in July 2018 before it came right back down. Ether, in the same video, is already up about 31% in August, the first green August they have had. That is color on red August. It is not a grade.

Jordi restated last week's 22% / seven-sigma / 200-day week in The Silent IPO Is Over on August 24, and named the sentiment symmetry of its $58,000 low. That combination has appeared only twice in the last decade. The pattern is evidence, never a mechanical price target. No new Fed date in that piece.

The Fed split is not wrong. The 10-year is the fade.

Sunday had September at 30.5% hike and 68.5% hold. This table close is 32.5% and 66.5%. Any hike in 2026 55.5% to 57.5%. Still a majority hold. A few points toward Ben. Not a 40% September hike. That 40% is not this table.

Year-end 4.0% 31.6% to 30.8%. Year-end 3.75% 42.8% to 43.0%. The crowd's modal year-end is still the current hold, not hold-after-hike at 4%. December remains Ben's second door. Jordi did not recut the September call this window.

A "raise at least once" line landed in an August 25 upload. It is Jason Pizzino, on an August 19 recording, about before the cycle ends. It is not Cowen, and it is not September.

10Y reaches 5.0% Sunday 23.5% to 16.5%. Range this window 15.0% to 26.5%. No spike like last week's 43.5%. No 10-year yield print in the table or in this week's corpus. Jordi's four-to-4.70 wedge is the tape the crowd is paying. Ben's 4.7 toward 5% looks wrong so far this window. Horizon is still year-end.

Wednesday 4:13 p.m. ET, CPI inflation above 3.6% jumped 23.0 points. That is a probability. The corpus never names PCE or CPI. Do not convert it into a print.

The ledger through Thursday

Sunday owns the ledger. Nothing is resolved. Two Sunday ADD lines (token 25 basis points in September or December then hold at 4%, and the year-end time-stop on a lower low) are still not in the book. Noting that is not adding them.

Ben, July 26: red August. Looks wrong so far. Still open. Five days. Grade Monday, September 1. He already said August 20 it was up 10% and not as likely. The 80,000 up-strike resolved. Ether's first green August is in his own mouth. It still needs a red monthly close. (2026-07-26-cowen-02)

Ben, July 26: rejected at the band, trades lower through August and September. Stressed. The tape went through the 75,000 and 80,000 up-strikes, not rejected below the band. He still has the 2018 give-it-back analog. Horizon September 30. (2026-07-26-cowen-01)

Ben, August 16: Bitcoin below 60,000 before the S&P correction. Weakness-first looks wrong so far. The 80,000 up-strike resolved. Down-to-60,000 is 28.5%. No S&P correction in the files. The correction clause has not started. (2026-08-16-cowen-01)

Ben, August 3 / August 6 / August 15: below 60,000 before the cycle low, cycle low September 20 to December 15, cycle low during the equity correction. Same tape, long horizons. If July 1 holds, those miss later. Pizzino still says July or October, who knows. (2026-08-03-cowen-01) (2026-08-06-cowen-01) (2026-08-15-cowen-01)

Jordi, August 16: new 2026 high above 70,000. Looks landed pending a spot series. The 75,000 and 80,000 up-strikes went to 0.9995 and left the feed. Stronger than Sunday. Still not a spot high. Do not grade it. (2026-08-16-visser-01)

Jordi, August 9: holds the 2026 low and breaks the bear range. Stressed toward landed. Same 80,000 resolution. Down-to-60,000 at 28.5%. The two-week / 200-day hold is still ahead. (2026-08-09-visser-04)

Jordi, August 9: no hike on September 16. Slightly more stressed. Still a majority hold. 30.5% to 32.5%. Warsh is Friday. Do not pre-grade. (2026-08-09-visser-03)

Ben, July 28: 10-year toward 5%. Looks wrong so far this window. 23.5% to 16.5%. Horizon year-end. (2026-07-28-cowen-04)

Ben, August 16: realized vol up from the August 16 lows by October 15. Still pending a series. Seven-sigma / 22% is the event, in the wrong units. Do not mark landed. (2026-08-16-cowen-02)

The rest of the 22 open claims did not get a new print: S&P local top by September 30, 10 to 20% second half, dollar year-end head-to-head still unpriced, gold June-to-October low aging well, July cleansing aging well, July AI low aging well, tech-momentum vol, high-multiple AI phase, hedge-fund leverage still no clean data.

The synthesis

Sunday's honest picture was a crowd that had already left Ben on Bitcoin and a Fed split that was still a hold. This window paid Jordi's breakout in the only language this table speaks. The 75,000 and 80,000 up-strikes resolved. Down-to-60,000 kept fading. Gold took points from the S&P. Ben's order, weakness first, rejection at the band, red August, is the side the tape ran through. Willing to say that looks wrong so far. Not willing to grade it.

The Fed split Sunday named is not wrong. September is 32.5% hike and 66.5% hold. Hike-in-2026 ticked up to 57.5%. Jordi's no-September-hike is slightly more stressed and still the majority. Ben's September-or-December door is still open. Jackson Hole has not printed.

The long end is no longer the clean agreement. The 5% line is 16.5%. Jordi's wedge is the one the crowd is paying this week. Ben's 5% call has a year-end horizon. It looks wrong so far in this window.

The two-week candle Ben dated from August 23 is the next Bitcoin clock. About August 30. Red August is Monday, September 1. Do not invent a Friday Warsh print from a Thursday morning file.

Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Written August 23, 2026, covering material published August 17 through August 23 and market prices through August 23.

  • Ben: the Fed delivers one 25 basis point hike in 2026, September or December, then holds at 4%. If Bitcoin makes no new cycle low by December 31, he will not call a lower low into 2027.
  • Jordi: stay long Bitcoin above the 200-day. Three candles through it, a 22% week, and he will bail only if it loses that average. He still sees no September hike unless Warsh is outvoted.
  • The tape: Bitcoin hits 80,000 went from 23.5% to 87.0%. Gets down to 60,000 fell from 80.5% to 34.5%. The crowd that picked Ben last Sunday flipped to Jordi, then ran.
  • The record: Ben 1-0 with 12 open. Jordi 0-1 with 10 open. Two new Cowen claims open this week. Nothing on the old book is graded. Scorecard

The pitch

Ben's strongest new line is a token hike, dated, then a hold. The August 17 video, The Rate Cutting Cycle is Over, is the one that belongs on the ledger. He names the size, the months, and the landing rate:

"We're talking about a token 25 basis point rate hike seems like a likely outcome to me."

— Ben, August 17, 10:01

"I think it'll either happen in September or December."

— Ben, August 17, 10:01

"I would argue it's probably going to happen this year and then after they raise rates, my guess is that they're then just going to hold at 4% for a little while."

— Ben, August 17, 18:32

That collides with Jordi's September-only no-hike claim. It does not collide with a hold in September and a hike in December. Paraphrasing the rest of that video: last NFP lost 23,000 jobs, unemployment is 4.1% from a 4.5% November 2025 high, and the 10-year is already back at 4.7% on its way toward 5%. The stock correction is still a 10 to 20% drop that does not start until September, maybe the very end of the month. Those are restatements of open IDs, not new ones.

The other new line is a time-stop on the lower-low stack. August 20, Bitcoin Rallies to the Bear Market Resistance Band:

"if Bitcoin's going to go lower before the next bull market begins, it'll happen before the end of the year, frankly"

— Ben, August 20, 5:28

"if we go for the rest of the year without a lower low, I don't think it would make sense to call for a lower low beyond that."

— Ben, August 20, 5:28

He has not abandoned a 2026 lower low. He has said when he will stop calling one. That is the claim.

He also owns the damage to red August, in his own voice:

"every midterm year, Bitcoin has gone down in August and right now it's actually up 10%. So what gives? Could Bitcoin go down in August? I mean, it's not as likely now as it was a week ago, that's for sure."

— Ben, August 20, 11:40

Paraphrasing the same tape: Bitcoin is below 70k and still down almost 50% from the highs, the rally from the low is about 20 to 22%, July 1 is the low so far, and they did get a daily close above the 200-day. He still wants a rejection at the bear-market resistance band. In Bitcoin: Dubious Speculation he puts the 2018 analog at mid-70s for this cycle, and he says if Bitcoin is still holding the 200-day in a couple more weeks the odds the low is in start to go up. That two-week test stays color. It is not a new ID.

August 18, The Market is Wrong About the US Dollar, is a restatement of the existing year-end dollar claim, with a 105 to 106 sketch. Color on 2026-08-05-cowen-02, not a second dollar row.

**Jordi's Sunday video, The AI Crypto Macro Nexus Point, is a process rule on the 200-day and a restatement of no September hike.** He is not adding a dated Fed claim. He is doubling down on the one he already has:

"there's no way I can see him raising rates unless he's outvoted. I just don't see how it's going to happen."

— Jordi, August 23, 19:07

On Bitcoin he will stay in the story until the average fails:

"from this point on until Bitcoin goes back under the 200 day moving average. That'll be the point that I bail out and say, Okay, I'm not talking about it anymore."

— Jordi, August 23, 3:03

The week he is describing:

"Three massive candles in a row breaking the 200 day moving average in Bitcoin."

— Jordi, August 23, 26:48

"We moved by 22% this week. So, you get a seven sigma move."

— Jordi, August 23, 29:51

He also says Bitcoin was up 23% this week. Sixty-day vol sat at 23 before the move. Prior weekly moves above 5 sigma: April 7, 2019 and January 15, 2023. That is the event Ben's August 16 vol-compression claim was waiting on. There is still no single realized-vol series to grade it against, so it stays open.

The Treasury tape, in his words, not as a Funnel print:

"the Treasury announces increased sizes of nominal end liquidity support, the most important news of the week, and helped get Bitcoin moving. Then, of course, he couldn't stop there. Oh, could be more than four billion."

— Jordi, August 23, 12:14

Paraphrasing the rest: gold had a 7% move back above its 200-day, which he reads as a debasement trade. The 10-year is a pegged wedge that they will keep managing, and he does not want the bet that it goes to 9 or 10%. His largest positions are now silver and Bitcoin. He cut AI in May and June. He still thinks the July lows are the lows, and he wants new highs in the thematic book by year-end as a grind, not a moonshot. Those last two stay color or restatements. They are not new IDs this week.

The backtrack

Twenty-two claims are open. None are graded. Confirm a mid-70s print and one vol series before anyone marks a land. What follows is pressure, not a score.

The Fed

Jordi, August 9: no hike on September 16. Still open, slightly stressed. Last Sunday this was aging superbly at 24.5%. This window walked toward Ben. September 25bp hike 24.5% to 30.5%, biggest +5.0 Monday 19:00Z. No change 74.5% to 68.5%. Any hike in 2026 46.5% to 55.5%. Still a majority hold. He restated it this Sunday. (2026-08-09-visser-03)

Bitcoin

Ben, July 26: red August. Stressed hard, eight days from the horizon. He said it himself: up 10% on the month, less likely than a week ago. Gets down to 60,000 80.5% to 34.5%. The month is not closed. It still needs a red August close. (2026-07-26-cowen-02)

Ben, July 26: rejected at the bear-market resistance band through August and September. Stressed. The tape went to the band. It was not rejected below it. He still says rejection means the same range-bound process. Horizon September 30. (2026-07-26-cowen-01)

Ben, August 16: Bitcoin below 60k before the S&P correction, correction mid-to-late September. Stressed. The order is what this week tested. Corpus has a 20 to 23% week, below 70k then through, mid-70s in the August 20 analog. The correction has not started, so the claim is not missed. The weakness-first clause is the part under pressure. (2026-08-16-cowen-01)

Ben, August 3: Bitcoin below 60k before the cycle low. Stressed, long horizon. Same tape. The new time-stop says a lower low, if it comes, comes in 2026. That complements this row. It does not retire it. (2026-08-03-cowen-01)

Ben, August 6: cycle low between September 20 and December 15. Stressed. "July 1st ended up being the low, at least so far." If that low holds, this window misses later. Not gradeable until a new low or year-end. (2026-08-06-cowen-01)

Ben, August 15: cycle low during the S&P correction, not ahead of it. Still open. No S&P correction this week. If July 1 is the Bitcoin low and stocks never correct, this misses later. (2026-08-15-cowen-01)

Ben, August 16: Bitcoin realized vol up from the August 16 lows (30-day 1.16%, 60-day 1.47%) by October 15. Looks landed, pending a vol print. Jordi has a 22% week and 7 sigma after 60-day vol at 23. Those units do not match the August 16 prints. Do not grade until one series is pulled. (2026-08-16-cowen-02)

Jordi, August 16: Bitcoin catches gold and silver and makes a new 2026 high above 70k. Looks landed, pending a mid-70s tape confirm. Ben's August 20 analog puts the current band in the mid-70s. Jordi has a 22 to 23% week through the 200-day. Hits 80,000 closed at 87.0%. No spot high is in this week's files. Confirm mid-70s on a tape before anyone marks it. (2026-08-16-visser-01)

Jordi, August 9: holds the 2026 low and breaks the bear range. Stressed toward landed. Three candles through the 200-day, and Ben has a daily close above it at the band. The two-week hold test is still ahead. (2026-08-09-visser-04)

Stocks

Ben, August 8: S&P local top and correction by September 30. Still open. No correction start in this week's files. He restated late September on August 17. S&P wins 2026 68.5% to 57.5% is a crowd move, not a 10% index print. Jordi said the market finished down for the week. That is one week. (2026-08-08-cowen-01)

Ben, July 28: S&P down 10 to 20% in the second half. Still open. Same. Restated August 17 as a non-recession 10 to 20% drop starting in September. (2026-07-28-cowen-05)

Jordi, August 2: late-July unwind was a cleansing event. Still open, aging well. End of July as the inflection, restated this Sunday. (2026-08-02-visser-01)

Jordi, August 9: July AI and tech low holds. Still open, aging well. "these lows to me are absolutely the low." (2026-08-09-visser-01)

The long end

Ben, July 28: 10-year toward 5%. Stressed both ways. He restated it: already 4.7, heading toward about 5%. After Bessent he still has the 10-year at 4.7, and the 30-year "didn't even drop that much." Reaches 5.0% spiked (range to 43.5%, +9.0 Tuesday 14:00Z) then faded 28.0% to 23.5% in this window. Midweek had it at 36%. Spike and fade. Reaches 4.8% 64.0% to 67.0%. Jordi now treats the 10-year as managed between 4.00 and 4.70. (2026-07-28-cowen-04)

Gold

Ben, August 5: gold's 2026 low inside June to October. Still open, aging well. Jordi has gold up 7% and back above the 200-day. The June low near $3,970 from the August 15 memo is not taken out in these files. (2026-08-05-cowen-01)

The dollar

Ben, August 5: dollar higher on December 31 than on August 9. Still open. Dedicated August 18 video, 105 to 106 sketch. Nothing on the watchlist prices DXY. (2026-08-05-cowen-02)

Jordi, August 9: dollar not higher on December 31. Still open. He treats the recent dollar drop plus Bessent as fuel for the debasement tape. Opposite Ben, still unpriced. (2026-08-09-visser-05)

Leverage and volatility

Jordi, August 2: tech-momentum vol structurally high. Still open. Restated as 45-year highs. No numeric print near 70 this week. (2026-08-02-visser-02)

Jordi, July 25: high-multiple AI phase over. Still open. No 5-to-7 baggers, fireworks over. Forward returns, not falsified by a grind. (2026-07-25-visser-02)

Jordi, August 1: hedge-fund leverage versus terminal value. Still open, no clean data. A crowded-name overlay is color, not gross leverage. (2026-08-01-visser-03)

Jordi, August 9: peak hedge-fund gross in July. Still open, no clean data. Same. (2026-08-09-visser-02)

The synthesis

Last Sunday the crowd picked Ben on Bitcoin. Midweek it flipped. This window blew through. Hits 80,000 23.5% to 87.0%, biggest hourly +12.5 Friday 09:00Z. Gets down to 60,000 80.5% to 34.5%. Midweek already had the first leg (80k 30.5 to 51.0, 60k 77.5 to 57.0). Friday Z was the second. Do not invent a spot high from that jump. The files have below 70k, then mid-70s, a daily close above the 200-day, and a 20 to 23% week. That is enough to say the tape is with Jordi's breakout and against Ben's weakness-first order. It is not enough to grade the above-70k high.

On the Fed they have split again, and Ben put a real claim on it. Last Sunday Jordi's no-September-hike was aging superbly and Ben's old 57% number had collapsed. This week Ben dated a token 25 basis point hike to September or December, then a hold at 4%. Jordi doubled down: no hike unless Warsh is outvoted. The crowd moved a few points toward Ben (September 25bp 24.5% to 30.5%, any-2026-hike 46.5% to 55.5%) and still prices a hold. September 16 is now a head-to-head. December is Ben's second door.

The long end is no longer the clean agreement it was. Both men still want yields contained or higher for different reasons. Ben restated 4.7 toward 5%. Jordi now says Treasury will keep pegging the wedge, "could be more than four billion," and he does not want 9 to 10%. The 5.0% Polymarket line spiked to 43.5% intra-window and closed 23.5%, under last Sunday's 31% and under midweek's 36%. The shared mechanism is still live. The crowd that was paying up for 5% faded it.

The dollar is still the cheapest disagreement on the board. Ben dedicated a video to a year-end bounce, 105 to 106. Jordi spent Sunday on debasement after a 7% gold move. Nothing on the watchlist prices DXY. Both claims stay open and untrackable from the table.

Ben's new time-stop is the honest thing in his Bitcoin book. He has not killed the below-60k stack. He has said that if 2026 closes with no new low, he will not take that stack into 2027. That is how a book that is under pressure stays gradeable.

Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Written August 20, 2026, following up the August 16 Sunday piece and covering market prices through August 20.

  • Sunday said: the crowd had picked Ben on Bitcoin, with the whole ladder sliding lower.
  • Since then: the whole ladder flipped up, and Ben himself owns that his red August call looks shaky.
  • The long end kept rising. 10Y reaches 5.0% is at 36%, the highest reading in the archive. Both men's convergence is aging well.
  • Jordi's debasement trade finally got priced. Gold gained four points and S&P lost four and a half in the cross-asset race.

What Sunday said to watch, and what happened

Sunday's cleanest line was the head-to-head: Ben wants a breakdown below 60k before stocks roll, Jordi wants the basement trade with Bitcoin catching up to gold and silver, and the tape had picked Ben. That read did not survive the week. Bitcoin rallied back to the bear market resistance band, and the whole Polymarket ladder moved up with it. BTC hits 80,000 went from 30.5 to 51.0, hits 75,000 from 50.5 to 70.5, and gets down to 60,000 collapsed from 77.5 to 57.0. The biggest hourly moves were Wednesday afternoon, the same day Ben published a video acknowledging the rally. In a week, the crowd crossed the floor and bet with Jordi.

Ben did not dodge it. His August 20 video, Bitcoin Rallies to the Bear Market Resistance Band, is the most honest thing he has said about his own call all year:

"If you look at midterm years, you can see that every midterm year, Bitcoin has gone down in August and right now it's actually up 10%. So what gives? Could Bitcoin go down in August? I mean, it's not as likely now as it was a week ago, that's for sure."

— Ben, August 20, 11:40

He is careful not to flip. The rally is up about 20 percent from the low, a daily close is above the 200-day moving average, and he walks the 2018 analog where Bitcoin sat at the resistance band the week of August 27 and then sold off. But the red August claim is now plainly on the defensive, and he says so in his own voice. The August 1 resolution date is now the most interesting line on the ledger.

The long end kept doing what both men said

The mechanism that held the Sunday piece together, the long end rising on soft data, kept working. 10Y reaches 5.0% rose from 24.5 to 36.0 over the window, with a single-hour jump of nine points Tuesday, and reaches 4.8% sits at 66.5. Sunday reported the 5.0% line at 31%, the archive high. It has since pushed to 36%. Ben restated the mechanism this week with a number attached:

"The 10-year yield is likely going to head higher. It's already back up to 4.7. I think it's going to head up to about 5%."

— Ben, August 17, 13:49

And he now frames the rate cutting cycle as over. His August 17 video, The Rate Cutting Cycle is Over, argues the hiking cycle has already begun overseas and that a token hike is coming here:

"The risk here is that the Fed actually has to raise interest rates before they can ever lower them again. We're talking about a token 25 basis point rate hike seems like a likely outcome to me."

— Ben, August 17, 10:01

The market is beginning to price the mechanism, if not the timing. Fed rate at end of 2026: 4.0%, the hike-and-hold outcome Ben describes, rose from 23.5 to 29.6, while 3.75% rose to 41.2. The September line is unchanged, still roughly 27 percent for a 25 basis point hike, but the crowd has started to price a hike by year end. That is exactly the shape of Ben's new call. Sunday's note that his Fed number had collapsed is being revised by the tape.

Jordi's debasement trade finally moved

Sunday flagged that the cross-asset market was still refusing Jordi's debasement trade, with gold stuck near 18.5 percent. That refusal ended this week. Gold wins 2026 rose from 19.0 to 23.0, S&P wins 2026 fell from 69.0 to 64.5, and Bitcoin wins 2026 ticked up to 13.5. The crowd is not yet on his side, but it is moving his way, and it moved the same week Bitcoin's own ladder flipped toward him. Sunday said the widest gap on the board was the market disagreeing with Jordi. That gap has narrowed.

The ledger through Thursday

Sunday owns the ledger and nothing is resolved, so this stays a status check.

Ben, July 26: red August. Looking shaky. Bitcoin is up roughly 10 percent in August and sitting at the resistance band. Ben's own "not as likely now as it was a week ago" is the best summary. The resolution date is September 1, a week and a half away, and it needs a red close. (2026-07-26-cowen-02)

Ben, July 26: rejected at the resistance band, trades lower. Unconfirmed but under pressure. The band is what Bitcoin rallied to this week instead of being rejected below it. The rejection has not happened. (2026-07-26-cowen-01)

Ben, August 3: Bitcoin trades below 60k before its cycle low. Aging poorly. The below-60k line collapsed from 77.5 to 57.0 as the ladder flipped up. Still open, still a long way from December 31, but this was the worst week it has had. (2026-08-03-cowen-01)

Jordi, August 9: Bitcoin holds its low and breaks out. Aging well for the first time. Sunday said the tape had picked against him. It has now picked for him, and he has a video from Ben describing the breakout level as reached. This is the most one-week turnaround on the board. (2026-08-09-visser-04)

Ben, July 28: the 10-year rises toward 5%. Aging superbly. The 5.0% line is at 36%, the archive high, and Ben named 5% as his target this week. (2026-07-28-cowen-04)

Jordi's debasement thesis vs. Ben's dollar-higher call: both moved this week. Ben doubled down, dedicating an August 18 video to the dollar going higher in the short term, to roughly 105 to 106, as the "final headwind for Bitcoin and the stock market before the end of the midterm year." Jordi's gold line gained ground in the cross-asset race. Neither is gradeable from the watchlist, which prices neither the dollar nor gold's path directly, so this stays a divergence to watch rather than a claim to score. (2026-08-05-cowen-02) (2026-08-09-visser-05)

The synthesis

The week's honest summary is that Sunday's clean picture came apart. Sunday presented a crowd that had picked Ben on Bitcoin against Jordi. It flipped. The most useful thing this piece can say is that Sunday's read is not aging well on the crypto side, and Ben has said it himself. But the two men's shared mechanism, the long end, is aging better than ever, and Jordi's gold trade finally got some price. So the scoreboard is messier than it was: the bond market keeps confirming both of them, the Bitcoin market just moved against Ben and toward Jordi, and the cross-asset race moved toward Jordi too. The one line that keeps both men honest is that nothing has resolved. Ben's red August still needs a red close, and Bitcoin is one rejected rally away from snapping back toward his breakdown.

The third voice

The table is one story. The Bitcoin distribution flipped from down to up, the long end kept rising, and gold took points from the S&P. Every column that Sunday said was pointed against Jordi moved toward him, and every line Ben leaned on for the correction is still intact on the bond side. The one tension left is inside Ben's own view: he needs the long end up for his correction mechanism, and he needs Bitcoin weak before stocks roll, but this week the long end rose and Bitcoin rallied with it. A bond rally and a crypto rally in the same week is the closest the tape has come to testing whether his two theses pull in the same direction.

The week ahead

  • September 1. Ben's red August claim resolves. Bitcoin is up roughly 10 percent on the month and needs a red close. This is now the highest-stakes line on the board.
  • September 16. The FOMC. Ben's rate-hike call and Jordi's no-hike claim collide here. The market still prices no change, but the year-end 4.0% line is climbing toward Ben.
  • Jackson Hole. Jordi flagged Warsh speaking there. Ben now leans on the same absence of forward guidance, calling it part of why the long end keeps rising.
  • The resistance band. Bitcoin sits at the bear market resistance band it has failed against repeatedly. A rejection snaps the week's flip back toward Ben. A hold and follow-through is the breakout Jordi has been waiting for.
  • The dollar. Ben published a dedicated video arguing it goes higher in the short term, to roughly 105 to 106. Nothing on the watchlist prices it, so this is a divergence to watch rather than a claim to score.

item.description: Soft CPI, a rising long end, and the week the tape picked Ben on Bitcoin
item.content:encoded:
Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Written August 19, 2026, covering material published August 10 through August 16 and market prices through August 16.

  • Ben: the S&P correction starts in mid-to-late September, and Bitcoin shows weakness first, trading below 60k before stocks roll. His August 15 memo put numbers on the whole thing: a 65% late-cycle base case.
  • Jordi: buy the basement trade. Gold and silver have moved, Bitcoin has not yet, and the dollar is already at new lows. The bond market will not rally even on soft data.
  • The tape: soft CPI crushed September hike odds to 24.5%, yet the 10-year broke higher and reaches 5.0% closed at 31%, the highest reading in the archive.
  • The record: Ben 1-0 with 12 open. Jordi 0-1 with 10 open. Scorecard

The pitch

Ben spent the week compressing two years of analogies into a dated, weighted forecast, and his written memo is the strongest thing he has produced all year. The August 15 report is more committed than anything in the videos. He puts the S&P at new all-time highs near 7,786, up 13.7% year to date, and names the mechanism that separates a correction from a recession:

"The labor market is what separates a correction from a recession, and it has not made the turn."

— Ben, August 15

He then states the whole thesis as a distribution, which is a first for him:

"The framework carries the view as a distribution: roughly 65 percent late-cycle base case, 20 percent deeper policy-error correction, and 15 percent recessionary transition."

— Ben, August 15

The valuation backdrop is the clearest he has stated: the Shiller CAPE at 41.2, second-richest in a century behind only 2000. And the call that ties Bitcoin to the equity move:

"its cycle low has historically formed during the equity correction rather than ahead of it"

— Ben, August 15

The August 16 video, The Winds of Winter, puts the date on the stock move:

"I don't really think that correction in stocks is going to happen until September, and probably not even until mid to late September. But normally, Bitcoin shows weakness before stocks do."

— Ben, August 16, 1:34

So Bitcoin breaks first, then stocks, then Bitcoin bottoms inside the equity correction. He is leaning on volatility compressing to a historic floor to time it. Sixty-day realized volatility is at 1.47%, 30-day at 1.16%, and he treats that as the trigger:

"within the next few weeks, volatility is likely going to pick up a lot."

— Ben, August 16, 10:50

The rest of the week is the same template restated. August 10 he called it crunch time and leaned down:

"I would lean towards breakdown because that's what it normally does near the end of midterm years, but only time will tell."

— Ben, August 10, 4:38

August 12 he put the seasonal ledger down, "on average Bitcoin drops about 10 to 11% in August and it drops about 8% in September," and the cycle low window in his usual words:

"I would say the odds the the low for Bitcoin based on the four-year cycle low, the odds are that it occurs between like late September and and and like mid December"

— Ben, August 12, 18:37

Paraphrasing his read of the next 60 days: the last three cycle lows landed on day 1432 and day 1436, Bitcoin is on day 1360, so the window is a few weeks out, which is why October remains his candidate month. His anchor:

"October to October makes the most amount of sense to me. If the market gives us to reason to pivot, I'll pivot."

— Ben, August 12, 20:09

August 14 was a product video, a new whale-watching dashboard, with one usable observation buried in it: whale transaction activity at the 100k, 1m and 10m size buckets is at levels not seen since August 2018, which he reads as confirmation of the low-interest, low-activity bear.

Jordi published his most ambitious paper of the year on Monday and his most quotable trade call on Sunday. The Monday Substack, The Yen Signal, argues that the late-July US-Japan coordinated yen intervention is the tell, a contextual signal rather than a single event:

"For the Fed and Treasury, we are running hot into a scarcity of tool options to fight long-term yields."

— Jordi, August 10

His frame for the long end, which is the exact observation that dominates the tape this week:

"Dollar Yen has become a new pressure point for the market to watch."

— Jordi, August 10

And the conclusion that names the trade:

"Gold's move this week may be the market's first acknowledgment that the solution to the debt problem will increasingly look like some form of debasement."

— Jordi, August 10

The Sunday video, AI Is Changing Time, opens with a headcount of the regime: S&P earnings up 51% year over year, sales up 15%, new all-time highs across the globe, his AI thematic portfolio up 3% on the week. On the Fed he is unambiguous:

"now we're down to 31% for September for Wor[s] and 80% for the BOJ. These numbers were about 5050 each before the payroll numbers."

— Jordi, August 16, 41:28

He calls the market's persistence wrong and names the trade:

"I happen to believe this is a mistake by the markets and you should be buying the the basement trade. You should be buying gold, buying silver, buying Bitcoin."

— Jordi, August 16, 41:28

The cleanest scoreable sentence in his week is the gap between gold and silver and Bitcoin:

"Gold has moved. Silver has moved. Bitcoin has not moved yet."

— Jordi, August 16, 48:27

Paraphrasing what follows: the dollar is already down at new lows, gold and silver have responded to the debasement regime, and Bitcoin is the line still sitting at the bottom that has not yet caught up. He wraps it with the central-bank confirmation, China adding 20 tons of gold in July:

"20 tons of gold in July, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023"

— Jordi, August 16, 49:15

The backtrack

Eighteen claims are open and none have reached their horizon, so none are graded this week. What follows is where each one stands. A claim that goes unmentioned is a claim being dropped, so every one of them appears.

The Fed

Jordi, August 9: no hike on September 16. Aging superbly, still open. September hike odds fell from 35.5% to 24.5% this week on soft CPI. He was shocked at 45% last week. It is now twenty points lower than the number that shocked him. This is the strongest open claim on the board. (2026-08-09-visser-03)

Ben's September-hike call, by contrast, has collapsed. He cited 57% on August 4 and 43.9% on August 8. It is 24.5% now. This was never a ledger claim of its own, but it is the load-bearing number under his correction timing, and he said at the time that the correction did not depend on it. It does not. The long end delivered instead, which is the mechanism that actually matters to him.

Bitcoin

Ben, July 26: red August. Still open, horizon September 1, and the crowd moved his way. Bitcoin closed the week near 62-63k. A week ago it was up on the month. The distribution has since slid the whole ladder lower, so the down-month case is more onside than it was. Too early to score, but it is no longer losing. (2026-07-26-cowen-02)

Ben, July 26: rejected at the bear market resistance band, trades lower through August and September. Still open, horizon September 30. The band has fallen to roughly 69k while price sits near 62-63k, so the rejection still has not been tested. Ben repeated the breakdown expectation three times this week. Nothing scored. (2026-07-26-cowen-01)

Ben, August 3: Bitcoin trades below 60k before its cycle low is in. Still open, horizon December 31, and the tape moved toward it. Bitcoin gets down to 60,000 rose from 75.5% to 80.5% and gets down to 45,000 rose to 24.5%. The downside is being priced. (2026-08-03-cowen-01)

Ben, August 6: cycle low prints between September 20 and December 15. Still open, horizon December 31. Restated almost verbatim on August 12. Unchanged, well sourced. (2026-08-06-cowen-01)

Jordi, August 9: Bitcoin holds its low and breaks out rather than making a lower low. Still open, horizon December 31, and this was a bad week for it. The crowd went against him. The whole Bitcoin ladder moved down and the breakout is not being priced. He is not wrong yet, but the tape has picked the other side. (2026-08-09-visser-04)

Stocks

Ben, August 8: the S&P sets a local top and corrects by September 30. Still open, horizon September 30. The index made new all-time highs near 7,786 this week. Nothing has started. He repeated the timing on Sunday, mid-to-late September, so this is exactly where his own calendar says it should be. Nothing to score. (2026-08-08-cowen-01)

Ben, July 28: the S&P falls 10-20% from its high starting in the second half of 2026. Still open, horizon December 31. New highs all week. The drawdown has not started. (2026-07-28-cowen-05)

Jordi, August 2: the late-July unwind was a cleansing event, not a sustained decline. Still open, horizon October 31, and aging very well. New all-time highs across the US, the DAX and the FTSE, and his AI basket up 3% on the week. The rebound has held for three weeks. This is a candidate to land. (2026-08-02-visser-01)

Jordi, August 9: the July low in the AI and technology complex holds, and neither takes out the July lows. Still open, horizon December 31, and aging very well. Same evidence, the tape at new highs. (2026-08-09-visser-01)

The long end

Ben, July 28: the 10-year yield rises toward 5% following the July hold. Still open, horizon December 31, and this was its best week in a month. Reaches 5.0% rose from 21.0% to 31.0%, the highest in the archive, and reaches 4.8% sat at 64.0%. The move happened in the Monday night Asian session, before CPI, and soft CPI did not bring it back down. This claim is back in the strongest shape it has been in since the first week of August. (2026-07-28-cowen-04)

Gold

Ben, August 5: gold's 2026 low is set inside the June-to-October window and gold does not make a new low after October 31. Still open, horizon December 31. His August 15 memo restates it: gold spiked to a late-January high near $5,560, faded to a late-June low near $3,970, and recovered toward $4,370, which he reads as a midterm reset rather than a top. Consistent. (2026-08-05-cowen-01)

Jordi's debasement thesis sits against a crowd that is still not buying it. Gold wins 2026 closed at 18.5%, down a point, and S&P wins 2026 at 69.0%. Gold did not rally this week to back him, but his new claim below is the line the ledger can actually grade.

The dollar

Ben, August 5: the dollar is higher on December 31 than on August 9. Still open. Jordi, August 9: the dollar is not higher on December 31. Still open. Nothing on the watchlist prices the dollar, so neither can be tracked from market data, exactly as flagged last week. Jordi said Sunday the dollar is "already down here at new lows," which is consistent with his side. Ben's memo keeps a bullish lean on the presidential-term analog. Neither is gradeable from the tape. (2026-08-05-cowen-02) (2026-08-09-visser-05)

Leverage and volatility

Jordi, August 2: realized volatility on the tech momentum factor stays structurally above its pre-2026 highs near 70. Still open, horizon December 31. No clean read this week, and his own AI basket at new highs cuts against the vol staying high. Unchanged. (2026-08-02-visser-02)

Jordi, July 25: the high-multiple phase of the AI trade is finished, with no repeat of 7-8x returns. Still open, horizon December 31, and aging poorly. His thematic basket kept making new highs and returned a portfolio up 94% on the year for the 10-name version. The claim is about forward returns, so nothing is falsified, but three weeks of this is not evidence for it. (2026-07-25-visser-02)

Jordi, August 1: rising leverage into falling terminal-value confidence is structural, and gross exposure does not return to prior highs. Still open, horizon December 31. No clean data, and it now partly contradicts his peak-gross-leverage call below. Unchanged. (2026-08-01-visser-03)

Jordi, August 9: hedge fund gross leverage peaked in July 2026 and does not make a new all-time high. Still open, horizon December 31. No clean data. Unchanged. (2026-08-09-visser-02)

The synthesis

The two men's mechanisms converged on the long end this week, and the tape delivered for both of them. This is the rarest and most useful thing in the archive: an agreement, and a confirmed one. Ben's mechanism is that if the Fed does not hike, the long end breaks higher and does the Fed's tightening work, which is what corrects stocks. Jordi's mechanism is that the debt burden means the long end will not fall no matter what the data says, which forces the authorities toward debasement. Both predict the same thing: the 10-year yield rises. This week soft CPI landed and the 10-year went up anyway. That is the exact observation, and both of them described it in advance. Jordi said it most directly:

"We had a week where the inflation data surprised on the downside. Retail sales missed. We had a week before where the jobs number missed. And yet long-term yields are just not coming down."

— Jordi, August 16, 40:43

Hold that against Ben's rising-yields mechanism and you get the same event explained two ways that do not contradict each other. When that happens, it is worth saying plainly: this week they were on the same side of the bond market.

On the Fed they have quietly converged too, and it is a one-sided result. Jordi has been no-hike all along. Ben cited 57% for a September hike on August 4 and the number has collapsed to 24.5%. Jordi was right and Ben's number was wrong. But Ben's correction never needed the hike, and the long end has delivered the mechanism he did need. So the convergence on the long end is what lets Ben's core thesis survive his failed Fed call.

The disagreement is Bitcoin, and this week the crowd picked Ben. Ben wants a breakdown below 60k, Bitcoin showing weakness before stocks, and a cycle low formed inside the equity correction. Jordi wants the basement trade, with Bitcoin eventually catching up to gold and silver. Both cannot be right about the direction of the next three months. The market moved the whole Bitcoin ladder down this week, which is a bet with Ben and against Jordi. That is the clean head-to-head, and it is now priced.

The dollar is the one line they still hold exactly opposite, and it remains the cheapest disagreement on the board because nothing on the watchlist prices it. Ben says begrudgingly higher into year-end, Jordi says already broken down and fueling gold and silver and Bitcoin. Jordi repeated his side on Sunday. Both claims sit in the ledger and will be graded off the index directly.

The third voice

The long end breaking higher on soft CPI is the story of the week, and it lines up with both men. 10Y reaches 5.0% rose from 21.0% to 31.0%, and the biggest single-hour move was +9.0 at Monday 23:00Z, in the Asian session, the same pattern as the prior week. The 6.0% strike took +5.0 at Tuesday 04:00Z. Then CPI printed soft on Wednesday and the long end did not come down. That is the tension the whole week was built on, and it is exactly the mechanism both men had already named.

The Fed repriced toward Jordi. September 25bp hike fell from 35.5% to 24.5% and any hike in 2026 fell from 54.5% to 45.5%. Fed rate at end of 2026: 3.75%, the no-move-at-all outcome, rose from 34.8% to 40.1%. The crowd is now most of the way to Jordi's no-hike view.

Bitcoin's distribution slid lower all week, a bet with Ben and against Jordi.

Bitcoin hits 75,000 fell 12 points and hits 70,000 fell 7, while gets down to 60,000 rose to 80.5%. The whole ladder is now lower than it stood a fortnight ago, and Ben's red August and below-60k calls are being priced in real time.

And the cross-asset market is still refusing Jordi's debasement trade. Gold wins 2026 closed at 18.5%, down a point, and Bitcoin wins 2026 at 12.5%, down a point. The crowd still calls this a rate move, not a regime move. Jordi spent two documents arguing it is a regime move, and the cheap expression of that thesis is unchanged: the market disagrees with him, and it is the widest gap on the board.

The week ahead

  • September 1. Ben's red-August claim resolves. Bitcoin closed the week near 62-63k and the distribution now points down, but the month is still only half over and Bitcoin needs a red close.
  • September 16. The FOMC. Jordi's no-hike claim resolves. The market is at 24.5% and falling. Ben's Fed call is effectively settled against him already.
  • Jackson Hole. Jordi flagged Warsh speaking there and the possibility that PCE is dropped as the primary inflation metric as soon as January. Watch whether Warsh gives any guidance, because the two-year is drifting on nothing else.
  • The long end. Reaches 5.0% is at the archive's highest reading, and both men want it higher for different reasons. A break above 5% is Ben's correction trigger and Jordi's debasement confirmation at once.
  • Mid-to-late September. Ben's correction window. The new claim carries the ordering: Bitcoin shows weakness first, below 60k, before stocks roll.
  • Volatility. Ben's claim that Bitcoin's realized volatility picks up sharply within the next few weeks is now in the ledger. Thirty-day vol at 1.16% is his canary.

item.title: Midweek: the CPI print did less than Sunday expected, and the bond market did all the work
item.dc:creator: CoJo Brain
item.description: Midweek: the CPI print did less than Sunday expected, and the bond market did all the work
item.content:encoded:
Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Midweek recap, covering Sunday afternoon through Thursday August 13, 11:00Z. It grades Sunday against the tape and opens no claims.

Sunday's week-ahead had six things on it. Two have resolved, one resolved in the opposite direction from the one this piece implied, and the one that mattered most was not on the list at all.

What Sunday got wrong

The long end broke higher on Monday night and Sunday never mentioned it. This is the miss.

Sunday's read was that the August 7 payroll print had knocked Ben's 10-year thesis back, and it said so: 10Y reaches 4.8% had fallen from 67.0% to 56.5%, and the claim behind it had "given a fifth of that back." Three sessions later the entire move is gone and then some.

marketSun closenowchange
10Y reaches 4.8%62.5%68.5%+6.0
10Y reaches 5.0%21.0%27.0%+6.0
10Y reaches 5.2%10.9%15.2%+4.3
10Y reaches 6.0%2.5%5.5%+3.0
10Y falls to 3.9%20.9%11.5%-9.4

Look at when it happened. The 5.0% strike took +9.0 in the hour at Monday 23:00Z, the 5.2% strike took +4.2 in the same hour, the 6.0% strike took +5.0 at Tuesday 04:00Z, and the 4.8% strike took +5.0 at Tuesday 08:00Z. Those are Asian session hours. Nothing American printed in that window. This was the Japanese long end pulling the Treasury curve with it, and it happened before CPI, not after.

10-year reaches 5.0% at 27.0% is the highest reading in the archive. It was 12.5% on July 26, 24.5% on August 2, 17.5% on August 9. Ben's most-repeated call of the year has never been better priced.

That matters twice over. It is the strongest week the tape has given 2026-07-28-cowen-04, and it is the mechanism that feeds his September correction: he has said all along that if the Fed does not hike, the long end goes instead. So far the long end is going without waiting to find out.

It is also, awkwardly for Sunday's framing, the thing Jordi wrote about on Monday. His paper is about exactly this pressure point:

"For the Fed and Treasury, we are running hot into a scarcity of tool options to fight long-term yields."

— Jordi, August 10

"Dollar Yen has become a new pressure point for the market to watch."

— Jordi, August 10

He published that Monday. The Treasury curve gapped in the Asian session Monday night. Sunday cast the yen intervention as the support beam under Jordi's no-hike case and left it there. The more interesting reading, visible three days later, is that Ben's rising-yields mechanism and Jordi's fiscal-trap mechanism are the same observation pointed at different conclusions, and this week the observation fired.

What Sunday got right, but smaller than it said

CPI landed Wednesday and it was not soft. It was in line with the hot tail cut off. Sunday's line was that a soft print "buries the September hike." Half of that happened.

The year-over-year ladder now reads 3.2% at 83.5%, 3.3% at 66.5%, 3.4% at 33.5%, 3.5% at 17.5%, 3.6% at 7.0%. That is a clean distribution centered just above 3.3%. What actually died on Wednesday was the upside: above 3.4% fell 17 points, above 3.5% fell 9, above 3.6% halved. The central case barely moved.

And the Fed barely moved with it. September 25bp hike went from 35.5% to 32.5%, three points, with -4.0 in the hour at Wednesday 13:00Z. Not a burial. A shrug.

The real Fed move was one meeting further out. Fed rate at end of 2026: 3.75%, which is the no-move-at-all outcome, went from 34.8% to 45.2%, and 4.0% fell from 35.5% to 23.2% with -7.2 at Wednesday 15:00Z. Meanwhile any hike in 2026 sat dead flat at 54.5% all week.

Hold those two side by side, because they do not fully agree. The crowd raised the odds the funds rate ends the year unchanged by ten points while leaving the odds of some hike this year untouched. Read charitably, that is the crowd moving a hike out of September and into a December that then gets reversed or never delivered. Read less charitably, one of the two markets has not caught up. Either way, Jordi's specific claim (2026-08-09-visser-03, no hike on September 16) is about the September meeting only, and it is getting better, not worse.

Worth naming what this does to Ben. He cited 57% on August 4 and 43.9% on August 8. It is 32.5% now. His September Fed call is the weakest thing he is carrying, and the correction he built on top of it does not depend on it, which he was careful to say at the time.

Bitcoin: Sunday's read was noise, and it retraced completely

Sunday said the Bitcoin distribution had "shifted up in a week both men called a bear market," and called it a modest bet against Ben's red August and with Jordi's breakout. All of it is gone.

The 70,000 line is back at 67.5%, exactly where it opened last week. The 60,000 line is back at 79.5%, within a point of where it opened last week. Three sessions erased a full week's move in both directions. Sunday treated a four-point drift as a signal. It was not one, and future weeks should want more than four points before calling a distribution shift.

Ben published twice into that and hardened. Monday:

"I would lean towards breakdown because that's what it normally does near the end of midterm years, but only time will tell."

— Ben, August 10, 4:38

"We are pre that event in my opinion."

— Ben, August 10, 3:51

Wednesday he put numbers on the window and restated the bottom range verbatim:

"on average Bitcoin drops about 10 to 11% in August and it drops about 8% in September"

— Ben, August 12, 3:05

"the odds the the low for Bitcoin based on the four-year cycle low, the odds are that it occurs between like late September and and and like mid December"

— Ben, August 12, 18:37

That is 2026-08-06-cowen-01 said again, six days later, in the same words. The claim is unchanged and better sourced than it was.

One open claim is offside and Ben pre-empted the objection himself. Bitcoin traded 63.5k Monday and 63k Wednesday, and it is up on the month so far, which puts 2026-07-26-cowen-02, the red-August call, on the wrong side with about eighteen days to run. He addressed it directly:

"you might say, well, right now, Bitcoin is actually up this month. But so what, right?"

— Ben, August 12, 2:19

Paraphrasing the rest: Bitcoin was also up in the first week or two of August 2022 and gave it all back into mid-September. That is a fair rejoinder and it is not a resolution. The claim is live, it is currently losing, and September 1 settles it.

He also opened a door he had not opened before, which is the scenario that would hurt him without ever falsifying anything:

"what if volatility dies out and we don't go up, we also don't go down."

— Ben, August 12, 16:16

His own answer is to hold the line and say when he would drop it:

"October to October makes the most amount of sense to me. If the market gives us to reason to pivot, I'll pivot."

— Ben, August 12, 20:09

Gold: Sunday's best observation is still standing

Sunday flagged that gold rallied 7.2% and Gold wins 2026 closed the week at exactly where it opened, and read that as the crowd calling it a rate move rather than a regime move. Five sessions on, gold is 19.5% to 19.0%. Still nothing. S&P wins 2026 is flat at 68.5% and Bitcoin slipped from 13.5% to 12.5%.

Jordi spent Monday's paper arguing the opposite, and it is the sharpest thing in it:

"Gold’s move this week may be the market’s first acknowledgment that the solution to the debt problem will increasingly look like some form of debasement."

— Jordi, August 10

The tape has now had five sessions to agree with him and has moved half a point the wrong way. That disagreement is unchanged and still the cheapest available expression of his thesis.

Two things not to read

The Kalshi growth ladder went incoherent on Wednesday and is not used here. Above 3.5% real GDP rose 5.0 points while above 3.0% fell 13.0 and above 4.0% fell 8.5, in the same hours. A single distribution cannot do that. The signature is the underlying event rolling to a new quarter rather than a repricing, so the growth and unemployment ladders are set aside this week rather than reported as a downgrade. Same for the August month-over-month CPI ladder, which is non-monotonic across strikes. The year-over-year CPI ladder above is clean and is the only inflation reading used.

The dollar is invisible to us. Sunday's closing bullet was that Ben and Jordi hold exactly opposite dollar claims. Nothing on the watchlist prices the dollar, so 2026-08-05-cowen-02 and 2026-08-09-visser-05 cannot be tracked between now and December from market data. They will have to be graded off the index directly. Flagging it now rather than discovering it on December 31.

Into the weekend

  • The Asian session. Monday and Tuesday's overnight hours moved the US long end more than the CPI print did. If that repeats, Ben's September correction arrives through the bond market rather than through the Fed, and it arrives earlier than his own calendar wants.
  • Bitcoin's month. Up so far, needs to be down by September 1, and Ben's own 2022 analog has the giveback starting right about now.
  • Whether the hike keeps leaking out of September. 32.5% and falling on the meeting, 54.5% and flat on the year. One of those two has to move.
  • Gold. Ben's gold low is in and Jordi's debasement thesis both want the same thing to happen. The cross-asset market wants neither. This is the widest gap between the two of them and the crowd on the board.

item.title: A 23,000 payroll print, and the week the two of them finally contradicted each other

item.description: A 23,000 payroll print, and the week the two of them finally contradicted each other
item.content:encoded:
Synthesized from what Benjamin Cowen and Jordi Visser published this week. They have not spoken to each other and did not participate. Quotes are verbatim and linked; everything else is labeled paraphrase.

Written August 10, 2026, the day after the week closed. It uses only material published on or before August 9 and market prices through that date.

  • Ben: the S&P correction starts by late September at the latest, and Bitcoin goes below 60k before the cycle low is in.
  • Jordi: the crash is over, the bottom is in, and he is shocked anyone still prices a September hike.
  • The tape: a 23,000 payroll print took September hike odds from 57.5% to 35.5%, fifteen points of it in a single hour.
  • The record: Ben 1-0 with 9 open. Jordi 0-1 with 9 open. Scorecard

The pitch

Ben spent five videos putting a date on the same forecast, and by Saturday he had the mechanism too. The clearest statement came after the payroll report:

"I would look for a correction to start by late September at the latest in line with prior midterm years, 2014, 2018, 2022."

— Ben, August 8, 25:31

He built that out of three dates. The 2014 correction started September 19. The 2018 correction started September 21. The 2022 top was August 16. The next Fed meeting is September 16. On Tuesday, with the S&P at 7750 and making new all-time highs, he laid out the fork:

"You're looking at about a 57% chance of a rate hike, a 43% chance that they do absolutely nothing."

— Ben, August 4, 6:09

And he made the fork not matter:

"If the Fed were not to raise rates in September, then the argument would simply be that the long end of the yield curve is going to go higher. You're likely going to have the 10-year yield breaking out above 5%."

— Ben, August 4, 7:42

Hike and equities de-rate on fear the easing cycle is over. No hike and the long end revolts. Either branch gets him his correction.

On Bitcoin he is now working a squeeze, not a level. Monday's video is eight minutes long and has one idea in it. The bear market resistance band is coming down through 69k, the 200-week moving average is coming up through 63.7k, and price is between them at 63.5k:

"Are we going to break above the bear market resistance band, or are we going to break below the 200-week moving average?"

— Ben, August 3, 1:36

He says which way he expects it to break:

"I can't begin to tell you, you know, exactly what week it's going to occur before Bitcoin likely heads back down below 60K."

— Ben, August 3, 3:10

The seasonal case behind it is the same one he has run all year, and this week he gave the full ledger:

"every prior midterm year was red for August. Negative 15% in 2022, negative 15% in 2018, negative 18% in 2014, even in 2010, negative 5%."

— Ben, August 3, 5:28

Thursday's cycle video adds the timing. Bitcoin is on day 1354 measured from the 2022 low, against cycles that ran 1430 to 1440 days, and on day 304 of a bear market that has averaged 406 days from the peak.

"my guess is that Bitcoin will bottom when it normally bottoms"

— Ben, August 6, 12:24

That window, in his words, is "late September through mid December," and his summary of the whole exercise is that

"I would say we are in the back 30% of the of the bare market."

— Ben, August 6, 17:49

Then Friday's jobs report arrived and Ben spent 28 minutes explaining why it does not mean what it looks like. Non-farm payrolls came in at 23,000 against roughly 80,000 expected, and the unemployment rate fell anyway, to 4.1% from 4.5% last November. His resolution:

"it is true that you don't have as many jobs, but there's also not as many people looking for a job."

— Ben, August 8, 7:01

Labor force participation has fallen from 62.5% to 61.4% since November. Paraphrasing the rest of his read: layoffs are only back at pre-pandemic levels, initial claims printed 189,000 a few weeks ago, and the weakness is a hiring freeze rather than a firing cycle. His line in the sand:

"as long as initial claims are below 300K, we're just not in a recession."

— Ben, August 8, 23:11

He also watched his own Fed number move against him inside four days, and said so:

"There's only about a 43.9% chance as it stands right now that you're going to get a rate hike in September."

— Ben, August 8, 17:49

Two smaller Cowen calls that are easy to miss and are both scoreable. On gold, down about 30% from its high, he refuses to turn:

"if the bull market's intact, which I still think it is, not financial advice, I still think it is, then the June to October time frame is when you would expect a bottom to occur."

— Ben, August 5, 6:57

And on the dollar, which is the hinge under everything else he said this week:

"the dollar in 2026 looks a lot like the dollar in 2018 where it just kind of begrudgingly goes higher."

— Ben, August 5, 5:27

Jordi published the week's most ambitious piece of writing on Tuesday and its most consequential call on Sunday. Take the call first, because it is the one that can be graded:

"It's over. The bottom is in as far as I'm concerned on a probability basis. If we take out the lows, I'd be surprised."

— Jordi, August 9, 13:56

The evidence he wanted was follow-through, and he got it. The four-day rally on the Nasdaq ran close to 10%. The S&P was up 3.6% on the week and made new all-time highs, as did the equal-weight S&P, the Russell, the NYSE composite, the DAX and the FTSE. Seven-day realized volatility on the tech momentum factor collapsed. Paraphrasing his read of that collapse: falling factor vol means funds are hedged or have cut gross, anyone vol-targeting cannot re-lever, it is August and volume is thin, and everyone who is short this is about to be forced to chase.

Out of the same observation he made a structural call:

"I'm making the call that we are at peak gross leverage and that we will see leverage come down over the course of the next few years"

— Jordi, August 9, 15:28

On the Fed he is not just leaning the other way from Ben, he thinks the market is being silly.

"I'm shocked after this last two weeks that we still have a 45% chance of a rate hike in September."

— Jordi, August 9, 38:33

His mechanism is not the labor market. It is Japan. The US and Japan intervened jointly to support the yen, the first coordinated move since 1998, and Bessent is reportedly leaning on the Fed to expand the facility behind it. Paraphrasing his argument: if the Treasury needs the interest rate differential to narrow to keep Japan from selling treasuries, and it is asking the Fed for help to do it, a Fed hike works against the thing the Treasury just spent its ammunition on. He puts a larger frame on it:

"when the US is intervening in the Japanese currency market to help their treasury market, the fiat system might be in trouble"

— Jordi, August 9, 40:51

Which is how he gets to the trade:

"Gold's in a bull market."

— Jordi, August 9, 43:09

"the dollar's already broken down, but this is just fuel for the fire for gold and and silver and platinum and Bitcoin."

— Jordi, August 9, 43:54

Gold had its third-biggest week in sixteen years, up 7.2%, and closed back above its 50-day after the third-longest stretch below it on his data.

And on the labor market he is the mirror image of Ben, using Ben's own facts.

"Yes, there are low claims and the reason there's low claims, part of this is the labor force is coming down, but they never talk about that."

— Jordi, August 9, 45:25

"You can't tell me the labor market is good with those metrics."

— Jordi, August 9, 46:14

The metrics are the quits rate and Atlanta Fed wage growth back at 2019 levels, average hourly earnings at 3.2%, and aggregate weekly payrolls printing

"the weakest six-month rate of change on the aggregate weekly payrolls going all the way back to 2012 when you throw out the COVID time period"

— Jordi, August 9, 46:59

His causal story is AI. Paraphrasing: agents have already hit hiring and have not yet hit firing, the job creation is happening inside one-person AI-native companies that do not show up in the establishment survey, and healthcare is the only sector adding jobs at all.

The Tuesday paper is the best thing either of them published this week and it opens nothing scoreable inside the year. Worth saying plainly, because the ledger is what this archive is for. The Age of Abundant Intelligence and Scarce Bitcoin takes one observation, that factor volatility hit all-time highs in July while Bitcoin's realized volatility sat at cycle lows, and builds a regime out of it:

"The asset class built on forecastable cash flows turned violent. The asset with no cash flows at all went quiet."

— Jordi, August 4

The thesis compresses to four words:

"Fiat printing debases the money. AI printing debases the moat."

— Jordi, August 4

Paraphrasing the argument between those two lines: AI is compressing the duration of every corporate moat, which widens the confidence interval around terminal value, which raises the effective discount rate on distant cash flows even for companies whose current earnings never miss. That is why the doubt climbed from software to the model labs to the hyperscalers in a year while Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon were carrying roughly $1.7 trillion of contracted forward demand. His conclusion is that scarcity that no press can reach gets re-rated, and that

"Liquidity is an option on time."

— Jordi, August 4

It is a genuinely good paper. It also has no dates in it, which is why the claims below come from the video and not from the paper.

The backtrack

Nine claims were open going into this week. One is graded, and it is graded early.

Jordi, July 26: no straight-line recovery in tech momentum, and the second half is chop. Missed. He said it after an 8% momentum bounce week:

"I find very little chance that we go straight back up. If we did go back up, I think it's going to take some time. I think it'll take the whole second half of the year."

— Jordi, July 26, 3:03

Eight trading days later the Nasdaq had rallied close to 10% in four days, his own thematic portfolio was up 6.5% in its second-biggest week of the year, and the S&P, the equal-weight S&P, the Russell, the NYSE composite, the DAX and the FTSE were all at new all-time highs. It went straight back up. The honest counter is that the horizon runs to December 31 and the second half could still turn choppy from here. That counter is being rejected because the operative content of the claim was the mechanism, not the calendar, and because the man who made it spent Sunday declaring the bottom in. Waiting until December to record that the first leg was wrong would be the exact thing this ledger exists to prevent. (2026-07-26-visser-01)

Jordi, August 2: the late-July unwind was a cleansing event, not the start of a sustained decline. Still open, horizon October 31, and aging very well. The follow-through he said he needed arrived in the first two sessions of the week and held. Factor volatility collapsed, the VIX went to its lowest since January, and CDX did nothing at all. This is the claim most likely to land of anything on the board. (2026-08-02-visser-01)

Jordi, August 2: realized volatility on the tech momentum factor stays structurally above its pre-2026 highs near 70. Still open, horizon December 31, and it is now fighting his own chart. Seven-day realized vol on tech momentum collapsed this week, and he showed it, approvingly, as the evidence the bottom was in. He restated the structural version anyway, saying he thinks factor vol does not go back down and that the rest of the year probably sits in a 25 to 30 band on his four-factor composite. That band is on a different scale from the 70 in the claim, so nothing is falsified yet, but the claim needs a specific measure named or it will be ungradeable in December. (2026-08-02-visser-02)

Jordi, August 1: rising leverage into falling terminal-value confidence is structural, and gross exposure does not return to prior highs. Still open, horizon December 31. He doubled down this week and put a name on it, calling peak gross leverage outright. Consistent, and now paired with a sharper claim below. (2026-08-01-visser-03)

Jordi, July 25: the high-multiple phase of the AI trade is finished. Still open, horizon December 31. A week in which his thematic basket posted its second-biggest gain of the year is not evidence against a claim about 7-8x returns, but it is not evidence for it either. Nothing to score. (2026-07-25-visser-02)

Ben, July 26: Bitcoin is rejected at the bear market resistance band and trades lower through August and September. Still open, horizon September 30. Bitcoin traded 63.5k on Monday and did not go near the band, which is now down at 69k. The rejection has not been tested. The band is falling toward price rather than price rising to the band, which is the squeeze his Monday video is about. (2026-07-26-cowen-01)

Ben, July 26: Bitcoin posts a red August. Still open, horizon September 1. One week in. Bitcoin was roughly flat and finished the week around the 200-week moving average. The crowd moved against him: Bitcoin gets down to 60,000 fell from 80.5% to 76.5% and hits 70,000 rose from 67.5% to 72.5%. (2026-07-26-cowen-02)

Ben, July 28: the 10-year yield rises toward 5% following the July hold. Still open, horizon December 31, and this was a bad week for it. 10Y reaches 4.8% fell from 67.0% to 56.5%. Reaches 5.0% fell from 23.5% to 17.5%. On the payroll print the market briefly priced a genuine easing scenario for the first time in a month, which is covered below. A fortnight ago this was the best claim on the board, up 48 points in ten days. It has given a fifth of that back. (2026-07-28-cowen-04)

Ben, July 28: the S&P falls 10-20% from its high, starting in the second half of 2026. Still open, horizon December 31. The S&P made new all-time highs at 7750 and finished the week up 3.6%. Nothing has started. He is comfortable with that and said so repeatedly, since his own template has the drawdown beginning in September, not August. (2026-07-28-cowen-05)

That leaves Ben 1-0 and Jordi 0-1.

The synthesis

Last week they were watching two different transmission channels and both were right. This week they read the same jobs report and came out on opposite sides of four separate questions.

On the labor market they agree on the fact and split on the meaning, and the agreement is more surprising than the split. Both of them identify the same mechanism, in the same week, independently: the unemployment rate is falling because people are leaving the labor force, not because anyone is hiring. Ben says it Saturday. Jordi says it Sunday, and adds that nobody says it, which is a slightly awkward thing to say the day after Ben said it on a macro channel with a large audience. He is not responding to Ben and there is no evidence either watched the other. But from there they invert. Ben stacks the low layoffs, the 189,000 claims print and the state-level unemployment map against the payroll number and concludes the economy is not rolling over, which lets the market keep climbing the wall of worry. Jordi stacks wages back at 2019 levels and the weakest six-month aggregate payroll change since 2012 and concludes the labor market is already bad and everyone is measuring it wrong. Same numerator, opposite verdicts, and the tiebreaker is whichever one of them is right about what happens when a hiring freeze meets a rate decision.

On the Fed the gap is 20 points wide and both men are quoting the same instrument. Ben cited 57% for a September hike on Tuesday and 43.9% on Saturday. Jordi cited 45% on Friday and called it shockingly high. So Jordi's "absurdly overpriced" and Ben's "coin flip" are two readings of nearly the same number four days apart, and the difference is entirely about direction of travel. Ben watched it fall and treated it as noise around a meeting that still matters. Jordi watched it stay up and treated it as the market failing to process a currency intervention.

On the correction the two of them are now flatly incompatible, and this is the fork of the year. Ben has the drawdown ahead of him, starting by late September at the latest, arriving on schedule with the Fed meeting, and ushering in Bitcoin's cycle low. Jordi has the drawdown behind him, finished in July, with the bottom in and the lows unlikely to be retested. There is no reading under which both are right. If the S&P puts in a local top in the next six weeks and rolls, Ben's midterm-year template survives a year in which almost nothing else about the market was normal. If the index grinds up through September on collapsing factor volatility and thin August volume, Jordi's positioning read beats Ben's calendar and the template breaks for the first time in four midterm cycles.

The counter each has against the other is worth naming. Ben's protection is that his correction does not need leveraged sellers, only a higher discount rate, which is why the dollar and the long end matter more to him than positioning does. Jordi's protection is that the mechanical fuel has already been burned, and that the fiscal and currency arithmetic now forces the authorities to step in before yields can do the damage Ben needs them to do. That is his "nothing stops this fiscal train" argument, and it is why he can be structurally bearish on public companies out to 2030 and tactically long the tape at the same time.

On the dollar they are exactly opposite and nobody is hedging. Ben expects it to begrudgingly grind higher, the way it did in 2018, and treats that as the headwind that finally cracks risk assets late in the midterm year. Jordi says it has already broken down and that the break is fuel for gold, silver, platinum and Bitcoin. Everything else they disagree about routes through this one line, and it is the cleanest head-to-head in the archive so far.

On Bitcoin they agree on the diagnosis and disagree on the resolution, which is rarer and more useful. Both call it a bear market right now, in the same week, in almost the same words. Ben expects the squeeze between the 69k band and the 63.7k moving average to resolve downward, below 60k. Jordi expects it to hold and break out. Note the precision, because it matters at grading time: below-60k and a new cycle low are not the same event. Bitcoin's low this year is near 57k, so Ben's call can land without Jordi's failing.

One last thing worth holding onto. Ben's closing thought on the cold card exploit, made in the same week that over $100m of self-custodied Bitcoin was drained, was not about the exploit:

"I got to believe there's going to be something that's going to make this cycle look exactly the same as every other cycle."

— Ben, August 6, 40:10

That is the whole method in one sentence, and it is also the method's weakness. Every event gets absorbed into the template. The template has been right for a year.

The third voice

The crowd repriced the Fed harder in one hour than in any hour since the July meeting, and it repriced toward Jordi. September 25bp hike fell from 57.5% to 35.5%, down 22 points on the week, with -15.0 in a single hour at Friday 13:00Z, the first hourly bucket after the payroll release. Any hike in 2026 fell from 67.5% to 54.5%, with -7.0 in the same hour.

Note the level, because both men missed it. Ben quoted 43.9% on Saturday and Jordi quoted 45% on Friday, both from wire sources. Polymarket closed the week at 35.5%. Jordi's argument that the hike is badly overpriced is correct and understated: this market is nine points below the number he called shocking.

Any hike in 202667.5%54.5%-13.0
10Y falls to 3.9%5.9%19.9%+14.0
10Y reaches 4.8%67.0%56.5%-10.5
BTC hits 70,00067.5%72.5%+5.0
BTC gets down to 60,00080.5%76.5%-4.0
